title: Liberation by Patton's army and his cousins' visit
summary: The camp was liberated in August 1944 by Patton's troops; Briggs's two cousins in that army visited him in Paris that fall.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Right, right up to about the 27th of August. We were liberated the 20th of August.
Yes, Patton's. I told you, I had two cousins
who were with him. I didn't see them, 'cause they were not in the group that liberated us, but I mean they were in the group that continued up to the Czechoslovakian border.
And those two cousins caught up with you then, after a little while?
Oh yes, yes. They came in the fall to Paris and they contacted me. They found out where I was.
They came on furlough to Paris?
So they knew you were in Paris?
They knew I was in Paris, yes. I had a few letters while I was in the camp. We were permitted to write one letter a month, and we would receive a letter "peut-etre" I'd say about one or
two letters a year. If you were fortunate, you'd receive three.
